title: Normal flow
learningObjectives: Explain normal flow and apply the layout behaviour correctly.

understand.concept: Normal flow is the default layout behaviour for block and inline content when elements are not taken out of flow or placed in another layout system. Block boxes generally stack in the block direction, while inline content flows within line boxes.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding normal flow helps explain why content moves when earlier content changes size. It is the foundation for using positioning, flexbox, and grid without unnecessary hacks.
understand.analogy: Normal flow is like paragraphs on a page: each block takes its place in sequence and later content follows it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; the browser uses formal formatting, containing-block, and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The headings and paragraphs appear in document order. Adding content to the first paragraph pushes later content down.

practise.guidedTask: Add another paragraph before the second heading. Observe how later content moves without positioning rules.

questions.prompt: What generally happens to later block content when an earlier block becomes taller in normal flow?
options: It moves farther down the page
questions.answer: It moves farther down the page
questions.explanation: Normal-flow layout places later content after the earlier block's used space.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to understand a layout behaviour?
options: Inspect the browser result and change one rule at a time
Assume every element uses the same containing block
Add z-index values without checking stacking contexts
questions.answer: Inspect the browser result and change one rule at a time
questions.explanation: A controlled experiment plus developer tools reveals the browser's actual layout behaviour.
